Closes #50

## What changed

- The Notifications page has a **Repository** and a **Type** filter. Both live in the query string (`repo=<id>`, `source=issue|pull|commit|repository`), so a filtered view can be bookmarked.
- The repository dropdown lists every repository I can access (owned, collaborator, team or org), plus watched repositories I have notifications from. A dot marks repositories with unread notifications.
- The filter applies to the list, the pager total, pinned rows, the Unread tab count, the per-row pin and mark-read buttons, and the live refresh. The navbar unread badge stays global.
- **Mark all as read** only marks the notifications that match the active filter, then returns to the same filtered view. To support this, `UpdateNotificationStatuses` now takes a `FindNotificationOptions` filter, which #51 can reuse.
- A filter with no matches shows "No notifications match the selected filters." with a Clear filters link.
- New model helper `FindNotificationRepoIDs` returns the distinct repository IDs of a user's notifications.

## Why

Users watching many repositories had no way to narrow the notifications list. This covers:
- AC1: filter by repository
- AC2: filter by type
- AC3: both filters together, on both tabs
- AC4: filters kept in the URL
- AC5: filtered empty state
- AC6: no other user's or private repository data exposed
- AC7: Mark all as read respects the filter

## How it was tested

- **Model unit tests** (`models/activities/notification_test.go`)
  - `TestUpdateNotificationStatusesFiltered` checks that a repo filter only marks that repo, that a filter matching nothing changes nothing, and that a caller-supplied `UserID` is ignored.
  - `TestFindNotificationRepoIDs` checks the distinct repo IDs.
  - The fixtures only contain issue notifications, so AC2 is covered here by source-filter cases (a non-matching type marks and lists nothing) and by the router test below; the positive "Pull requests" case was checked manually.
- **Router unit test** (`TestParseNotificationFilter`) covers valid, unknown and non-numeric `repo`/`source` values, and the redirect query string.
- **Integration test** (`TestNotificationFilters`, about 1s) has one subtest per acceptance criterion:
  - by repo (AC1)
  - by repo on the Read tab, with pinned rows (AC3)
  - empty state (AC5)
  - unread dot in the dropdown
  - an inaccessible repo ID exposes nothing (AC6)
  - Mark all as read respects the filter (AC7)

  It also checks that the filter links carry no stray `?`. I confirmed that check fails on the old template.
- **Manual checks** on a local Gitea with seeded test user
  - every acceptance criterion in the browser
  - the unread dots
  - paging with filters (27 notifications over 2 pages)
  - changing a filter from page 2 returns to page 1
  - the live refresh keeps the filter

## CI / manual verification

- `make lint-go`: 0 issues
- `make lint-js`: passes
- `make lint-templates`: 572 files, 0 errors
- `make lint-spell`: passes
- `./.claude-students/check.sh`: ok

- The `go test` runs for the model, router and integration tests above all pass.
- CI: still running when this was posted (e2e, checks-backend and lint-on-demand pass so far); I'll update this line when it finishes.

## Design

- Follows Design Decisions 1–3 in #50.
- Open questions:
  - The repository filter lists every accessible repository, with a dot on those that have unread notifications.
  - The navbar badge stays global, while the Unread tab count follows the filter.
- The type filter's query parameter is `source`, because `type` is already used for the Unread/Read tab.

Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5) helped plan the change and draft the model, router and template code and the tests, starting from concept location I did first (`notification.go`, `notification_list.go`, the `/notifications` routes, `notification_div.tmpl`). Part of #7.

### User Story

As a user who watches several repositories, I want to filter my notifications by repository and by type (issue, pull request, commit, repository) so that I can focus on what needs my attention without scrolling past unrelated updates.

### User Scenario

Dana watches a dozen repositories and has 80 unread notifications. She's about to review pull requests for `org/backend`. On the Notifications page she picks `org/backend` from a repository filter and "Pull requests" from a type filter. The list shows only pull request notifications from that repository, and the unread count reflects the filtered list. She copies the URL into a bookmark, and opening it later shows the same filtered view. Clearing the filters brings back the full list.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: Given notifications from several repositories, when the user selects repository R, then only notifications whose repository is R are listed.
- [ ] AC2: Given notifications of several types, when the user selects type "Pull requests", then only pull request notifications are listed.
- [ ] AC3: Given a repository and a type filter are both set, when the list loads, then only notifications matching **both** are shown, on both the Unread and Read tabs.
- [ ] AC4: Given filters are applied, when the page is reloaded or the URL is opened in a new tab, then the same filters are applied (filters are kept in the query string).
- [ ] AC5: Given a filter that matches nothing, when the list loads, then an empty-state message is shown instead of an empty table.
- [ ] AC6: Given a user tries to filter by a repository ID they have no notifications for or can't access, when the page loads, then no other user's notifications or private repository details are exposed.
- [ ] AC7: Given a repository or type filter is active, when the user clicks "Mark all as read", then only the unread notifications matching the filter become read, the others stay unread, and the filter is still applied on the page that loads afterward.

### Out of Scope

- Filtering by *reason* (mentioned, assigned, review requested, ...). Notifications don't store a reason today, so this needs a schema change; it will be a separate issue under #7.
- Bulk actions on notifications (#51).
- Saving or pinning filter presets.
- Changes to the notifications API (`/api/v1/notifications`).

### Open Questions

- Should the repository filter list only repositories the user currently has notifications from, or every repository they can access? (Proposed: every repository, but repos with unread notifications get an unread dot to show it)
- Should the unread-count badge in the navbar stay global, or follow the active filter? (Proposed: stay global.)

### Scope

medium

---
Drafted with Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5); Reviewed and changed by Carson.


### Design Decisions

**1. "Mark all as read" respects the active filter.**
Alternatives: (a) always mark everything read, ignoring the filter; (b) disable the button while a filter is active; (c) apply it to the filtered set.
Rationale: The action should apply to what the user is looking at. Clearing every notification when the user had narrowed to one repository is unrecoverable, and disabling the button removes the most useful case — triaging one repository at a time.
Consequences: The bulk update needs the same conditions as the list query; today `UpdateNotificationStatuses` only takes a user and a status. That seam is shared with #51, so it is decided here and reused there. The button label should make its scope clear when a filter is active.

**2. Pinned notifications are filtered like everything else.**
Alternatives: (a) always show pinned notifications regardless of the filter; (b) filter them like any other notification.
Rationale: A filtered view should answer the question the user asked. Pinned items from other repositories showing up under a repository filter would contradict the filter and make counts disagree with the rows.
Consequences: Pinned items can drop out of view while a filter is active and return once it is cleared. The query keeps the existing status set (current tab plus pinned) and adds the filter conditions on top.

**3. Filter lifetime and pagination behavior.** The filter persists while paging through results, is not carried beyond the notifications page, and changing a filter returns to page 1.
Alternatives: (a) keep the filter alive across visits through the session or browser storage; (b) keep the current page number when the filter changes.
Rationale: Leaving the notifications page and coming back should give a clean, unfiltered inbox. Keeping the page number risks landing on a page that no longer exists once the filtered result set shrinks.
Consequences: The `div-only` in-place refresh has to carry the filter parameters as well as the paging links. A user who always wants one repository bookmarks the filtered URL instead.

```text
# Course workflow — issues, PRs, reviews, sprint deliverables

Course rules, not upstream Gitea ones. Source: the course site <https://csci-435-se.github.io/>
(Sprints pages) and `docs/sprint0/standards.md`. Everyone on the team, and every AI session, uses
the formats below so all issues and PRs look the same. The GitHub templates in `.github/` carry the
same formats; if they ever disagree with this page, fix the template.

AI disclosure has its own page: `AI-ASSISTANCE.md`.

## Current sprint: Sprint 1
| D2 | Requirements spec for each issue (formats below), peer-reviewed by a teammate | 20 | Individual | Issue body |
| D3 | At least one non-trivial design decision per issue | 7 | Individual | Issue body |
| D4 | Code changes and PRs | 36 | Individual | PRs |
| D5 | AI logs | 7 | Individual | `ai-logs/sprint1/<github-username>/` |
| D6 | Sprint report | 10 | Team | `docs/sprint1/report.md` |
| D7 | Release: tag `v1.27.3-csci435-s1` plus a GitHub release | 2 | Team | Tags / Releases |
| D8 | Reflection survey | 8 | Individual | Blackboard/Zulip link |

- **D1 load:** each CSCI 435 student owns at least 2 medium issues; each CSCI 535 student owns at
  least 2 medium and 1 small. Every issue has exactly **one** assignee. Specs should be final by
  Sep 27.
- **D5:** conventions are in `ai-logs/README.md`. The folder must exist even if no AI was used. In
  that case, post an issue comment saying so. Log links go in **issue comments only**, never in PRs
  (`AI-ASSISTANCE.md`).
- **D7:** keep Sprint 0's base version (`v1.27.3-csci435-s0` → `v1.27.3-csci435-s1`), push the tag
  to origin, and write release notes listing the features, fixes and improvements.
- **Reviews:** each student reviews at least one PR per sprint. Over the semester, each student
  reviews every teammate at least once.
- **Extra credit:** up to 3 points per PR accepted by upstream Gitea.

## Branches and commits
or squashing after review has started is not allowed (`docs/sprint0/standards.md`):

```bash
git fetch origin
git merge origin/main
```

Do this before opening the PR and again if `main` moves while it is in review. Never merge another
feature branch into yours.

### After merge: clean up

A PR is merged with a merge commit once it is approved, every review comment is addressed and CI
passes. Then:

```bash
git switch main
git pull origin main
git branch -d feat/issue-<N>-short-description               # local branch
git push origin --delete feat/issue-<N>-short-description    # or GitHub's "Delete branch" button
git fetch --prune                                            # drop stale remote-tracking refs
```

Also check that the issue closed (via `Closes #N`), is on the sprint milestone, and has its AI
Assistance comment. Then run `specstory sync` and file the session's log (see `ai-logs/README.md`).

## Issue format: feature (user story)
- **Peer review (D2):** a teammate reads the spec and comments `Spec reviewed — <notes>` on the
  issue before implementation starts.

## Pull request format
explanation 5, description quality 4, CI or manual verification 3, review rubric posted 2.

## Code review rubric
The reviewer posts this as a **PR comment**, as well as the GitHub review itself. A copy-paste copy
is in `.github/code-review-rubric.md`, so keep the two in sync. Pull the branch and test it when you
can, say what you checked, and mark each point as required or optional
(`docs/community-governance.md`). Score each row against the issue's acceptance criteria. Anything
below 7 needs a note saying what would raise it.

```markdown
### Code Review — @reviewer-username

**Checked:** <what you ran or tried>

| Criterion | Score (1–10) | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Correctness — implements issue requirements | | |
| Test coverage — tests present and meaningful | | |
```

+// UpdateNotificationStatuses updates the statuses of all of a user's notifications that are of the currentStatus type to the desiredStatus.
+// filter narrows the update (e.g. RepoID, Source); its UserID and Status are always overwritten.
+func UpdateNotificationStatuses(ctx context.Context, user *user_model.User, currentStatus, desiredStatus NotificationStatus, filter FindNotificationOptions) error {
+	filter.UserID = user.ID // never let a caller widen the update to another user
+	filter.Status = []NotificationStatus{currentStatus}
 	n := &Notification{Status: desiredStatus, UpdatedBy: user.ID}
 	_, err := db.GetEngine(ctx).
-		Where("user_id = ? AND status = ?", user.ID, currentStatus).
+		Where(filter.ToConds()).
 		Cols("status", "updated_by", "updated_unix").
 		Update(n)
 	return err
 }
+
+// FindNotificationRepoIDs returns the distinct repository IDs of the notifications matching opts
+func FindNotificationRepoIDs(ctx context.Context, opts FindNotificationOptions) ([]int64, error) {
+	repoIDs := make([]int64, 0, 10)
+	return repoIDs, db.GetEngine(ctx).Table("notification").
+		Where(opts.ToConds()).
+		Distinct("notification.repo_id").
+		Find(&repoIDs)
+}

+	all, err := activities_model.FindNotificationRepoIDs(t.Context(), activities_model.FindNotificationOptions{UserID: 1})
+	assert.NoError(t, err)

+	none, err := activities_model.FindNotificationRepoIDs(t.Context(), activities_model.FindNotificationOptions{
+		UserID: 2,
+		Source: []activities_model.NotificationSource{activities_model.NotificationSourceCommit},
+	})
+	assert.NoError(t, err)
+	assert.Empty(t, none)
+}

+// notificationSourceParams maps the "source" query value to the notification source it selects
+var notificationSourceParams = map[string]activities_model.NotificationSource{
+	"issue":      activities_model.NotificationSourceIssue,
+	"pull":       activities_model.NotificationSourcePullRequest,
+	"commit":     activities_model.NotificationSourceCommit,
+	"repository": activities_model.NotificationSourceRepository,
+}
+
+// notificationFilter is the repository and type filter of the notifications page
+type notificationFilter struct {
+	RepoID int64
+	Source string // a key of notificationSourceParams, or "" for any
+}
+
+func parseNotificationFilter(ctx *context.Context) notificationFilter {
+	filter := notificationFilter{RepoID: max(0, ctx.FormInt64("repo"))}
+	if source := ctx.FormString("source"); notificationSourceParams[source] != 0 {
+		filter.Source = source // unknown values are ignored rather than matching nothing
+	}
+	return filter
+}
+
+func (f notificationFilter) IsActive() bool {
+	return f.RepoID != 0 || f.Source != ""
+}
+
+func (f notificationFilter) findOptions(userID int64) activities_model.FindNotificationOptions {
+	opts := activities_model.FindNotificationOptions{UserID: userID, RepoID: f.RepoID}
+	if f.Source != "" {
+		opts.Source = []activities_model.NotificationSource{notificationSourceParams[f.Source]}
+	}
+	return opts
+}
+
+// queryString is built from the parsed values, never the raw request, so redirects only carry validated input
+func (f notificationFilter) queryString() string {
+	q := url.Values{}
+	if f.RepoID != 0 {
+		q.Set("repo", strconv.FormatInt(f.RepoID, 10))
+	}
+	if f.Source != "" {
+		q.Set("source", f.Source)
+	}
+	return q.Encode()
+}
+
+// loadNotificationFilterRepos returns the repositories offered by the repository filter, sorted by full name,
+// and the IDs of those with unread notifications
+func loadNotificationFilterRepos(ctx stdCtx.Context, doer *user_model.User) (repo_model.RepositoryList, container.Set[int64], error) {
+	searchOpts := repo_model.SearchRepoOptions{
+		Actor:   doer,
+		OwnerID: doer.ID,
+		Private: true,
+	}
+	repos, _, err := repo_model.SearchRepositoryByCondition(ctx, searchOpts, repo_model.SearchRepositoryCondition(searchOpts), false)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, nil, err
+	}
+
+	// watched repos the user neither owns nor collaborates on are missing from the search
+	notifRepoIDs, err := activities_model.FindNotificationRepoIDs(ctx, activities_model.FindNotificationOptions{UserID: doer.ID})
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, nil, err
+	}
+	known := container.SetOf(repos.IDs()...)
+	missingIDs := slices.DeleteFunc(notifRepoIDs, func(id int64) bool { return known.Contains(id) })
+	if len(missingIDs) > 0 {
+		missing, err := repo_model.GetRepositoriesMapByIDs(ctx, missingIDs)
+		if err != nil {
+			return nil, nil, err
+		}
+		for _, repo := range missing {
+			perm, err := access_model.GetIndividualUserRepoPermission(ctx, repo, doer)
+			if err != nil {
+				return nil, nil, err
+			}
+			if perm.HasAnyUnitAccessOrPublicAccess() {
+				repos = append(repos, repo)
+			}
+		}
+	}
+	slices.SortFunc(repos, func(a, b *repo_model.Repository) int {
+		return strings.Compare(strings.ToLower(a.FullName()), strings.ToLower(b.FullName()))
+	})
+
+	unreadIDs, err := activities_model.FindNotificationRepoIDs(ctx, activities_model.FindNotificationOptions{
+		UserID: doer.ID,
+		Status: []activities_model.NotificationStatus{activities_model.NotificationStatusUnread},
+	})
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, nil, err
+	}
+	return repos, container.SetOf(unreadIDs...), nil
+}

+func TestParseNotificationFilter(t *testing.T) {
+	cases := []struct {
+		query    string
+		expected notificationFilter
+		active   bool
+		qs       string
+	}{
+		{"", notificationFilter{}, false, ""},
+		{"?repo=2&source=pull", notificationFilter{RepoID: 2, Source: "pull"}, true, "repo=2&source=pull"},
+		{"?source=unknown", notificationFilter{}, false, ""},
+		{"?repo=abc", notificationFilter{}, false, ""},
+		{"?repo=-5&source=commit", notificationFilter{Source: "commit"}, true, "source=commit"},
+	}
+	for _, c := range cases {
+		t.Run(c.query, func(t *testing.T) {
+			ctx, _ := contexttest.MockContext(t, "notifications"+c.query)
+			filter := parseNotificationFilter(ctx)
+			assert.Equal(t, c.expected, filter)
+			assert.Equal(t, c.active, filter.IsActive())
+			assert.Equal(t, c.qs, filter.queryString())
+		})
+	}
+
+	opts := notificationFilter{RepoID: 2, Source: "pull"}.findOptions(7)
+	assert.EqualValues(t, 7, opts.UserID)
+	assert.EqualValues(t, 2, opts.RepoID)
+	assert.Equal(t, []activities_model.NotificationSource{activities_model.NotificationSourcePullRequest}, opts.Source)
+}

diff --git a/tests/integration/notification_filter_test.go b/tests/integration/notification_filter_test.go
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..f185258eb4
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/integration/notification_filter_test.go
@@ -0,0 +1,77 @@
+// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
+// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
+
+package integration
+
+import (
+	"net/http"
+	"strings"
+	"testing"
+
+	activities_model "gitea.dev/models/activities"
+	"gitea.dev/models/unittest"
+	"gitea.dev/modules/test"
+	"gitea.dev/tests"
+
+	"github.com/PuerkitoBio/goquery"
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
+)
+
+func TestNotificationFilters(t *testing.T) {
+	defer tests.PrepareTestEnv(t)()
+
+	// user2 fixtures: #3 pinned (repo 1), #4 unread (repo 1), #5 unread (repo 2), #2 read (repo 1)
+	session := loginUser(t, "user2")
+
+	listedIDs := func(t *testing.T, query string) (ids []string, doc *HTMLDoc) {
+		resp := session.MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, "GET", "/notifications"+query), http.StatusOK)
+		doc = NewHTMLParser(t, resp.Body)
+		doc.doc.Find("#notification_table .notifications-item").Each(func(_ int, s *goquery.Selection) {
+			ids = append(ids, s.AttrOr("id", ""))
+		})
+		return ids, doc
+	}
+
+	t.Run("ByRepo", func(t *testing.T) {
+		ids, _ := listedIDs(t, "?repo=2")
+		assert.Equal(t, []string{"notification_5"}, ids)
+	})
+
+	t.Run("ByRepoOnReadTab", func(t *testing.T) {
+		ids, _ := listedIDs(t, "?type=read&repo=1")
+		assert.ElementsMatch(t, []string{"notification_2", "notification_3"}, ids) // pinned rows are filtered too
+	})
+
+	t.Run("NoMatchShowsEmptyState", func(t *testing.T) {
+		ids, doc := listedIDs(t, "?source=pull")
+		assert.Empty(t, ids)
+		assert.Contains(t, doc.doc.Find(".empty-placeholder").Text(), "No notifications match")
+		assert.Equal(t, "/notifications", doc.doc.Find(".empty-placeholder a").AttrOr("href", "")) // no stray "?"
+	})
+
+	t.Run("RepoDropdownMarksUnread", func(t *testing.T) {
+		_, doc := listedIDs(t, "")
+		item := doc.doc.Find(`[data-test-id="notification-filter-repo"] .menu a.item`).FilterFunction(func(_ int, s *goquery.Selection) bool {
+			return strings.TrimSpace(s.Text()) == "user2/repo2"
+		})
+		assert.Equal(t, 1, item.Length())
+		assert.Equal(t, 1, item.Find(`[role="img"]`).Length())
+
+		allRepos := doc.doc.Find(`[data-test-id="notification-filter-repo"] .menu a.item`).First()
+		assert.Equal(t, "/notifications", allRepos.AttrOr("href", ""))
+	})
+
+	t.Run("InaccessibleRepoIsNotExposed", func(t *testing.T) {
+		other := loginUser(t, "user5") // repo 2 is user2's private repo

  const newCount = await updateNotificationCount();

  } else if (timeout < notificationSettings.MaxTimeout) {

  }

    await updateNotificationTable();

async function updateNotificationTable() {
  const notificationDiv = document.querySelector('#notification_div');
  if (!notificationDiv) return;

  try {
    const params = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search);
    params.set('div-only', 'true');
    params.set('sequence-number', String(++notificationSequenceNumber));
    const response = await GET(`${appSubUrl}/notifications?${params.toString()}`);

    if (!response.ok) {
      throw new Error('Failed to fetch notification table');
    }

    const data = await response.text();
    const el = createElementFromHTML(data);
    if (parseInt(el.getAttribute('data-sequence-number')!) === notificationSequenceNumber) {
      notificationDiv.outerHTML = data;
    }
  } catch (error) {
    console.error(error);
  }
}

async function updateNotificationCount(): Promise<number> {
  try {
    const response = await GET(`${appSubUrl}/notifications/new`);

    if (!response.ok) {
      throw new Error('Failed to fetch notification count');
    }

    const data = await response.json();

    toggleElem('.notification_count', data.new !== 0);

    for (const el of document.querySelectorAll('.notification_count')) {
      el.textContent = String(data.new);
    }

    return data.new as number;
  } catch (error) {
    console.error(error);
    return 0;
  }
}

## Pull request format

Template: `.github/pull_request_template.md`. Title uses Conventional Commits, e.g.
`fix(issues): keep label filter after search`. Description sections:

1. `Closes #<N>`, which links the issue and closes it on merge.
2. **What changed:** the change in your own words.
3. **Why:** the problem, and which acceptance criteria (AC1…) it satisfies.
4. **How it was tested / Test strategy:** tests added or updated and why these ones. Name any
   change that can't be tested automatically and how it was checked by hand. Every behaviour change
   needs a new or updated test.
5. **CI / manual verification:** CI status, or the commands run and their results.
6. **Design:** one line pointing at the Design Decision in the issue, or a note on how it changed.
7. **AI assistance:** format in `AI-ASSISTANCE.md` §2, with **no log link**.

Per-PR grading (20 points): correctness against the acceptance criteria 6, test strategy with
explanation 5, description quality 4, CI or manual verification 3, review rubric posted 2.

## Code review rubric

## 2. A short section in the pull request description — no log link

Reviewers read the PR, and the review rubric scores "AI transparency", so the PR says how AI was
used and how you verified it. It does **not** link or cite the AI log: from Sprint 1 on, logs are
referenced in **issue comments only**, never in PR descriptions or PR comments (Sprint 1 page, D5).

Name the model, say what AI did and what you did, and point at the issue comment for the log.

## Rules that make a disclosure wrong

- **Placeholders left in**: `@your-github-username` or the full `Implementation / Code review /
  Testing / Other` list means the comment was pasted unread.
- **A log link in a PR description or PR comment.** Log links live in the issue comment only.
- **A log link that 404s.** Until the log is merged to `main`, link the branch that holds it; switch
  to the `main` link once merged.
- **A log folder that is not your GitHub username** — `ai-logs/sprint1/jdonohue/` is wrong when the
  account is `Jack-Donohue`.
- **Claiming work AI did as your own, or the reverse.** The claim must match the log.
- **AI-written replies to reviewer questions on your own issue or PR.** `CONTRIBUTING.md` forbids it:
  the questions are for you.

## For AI agents drafting an issue or PR

Put section 2 in every PR description you draft, and draft the section 1 issue comment
separately, both filled in from the session you actually ran — never with placeholders. You may
draft the wording, but say plainly that the human must review and edit it before posting, and leave
the issue comment for them to post under their own account.

import base64, json, time, urllib.request, urllib.error

BASE = "http://localhost:3002/api/v1"
CREDS = {"ai": "aiaiaiai", "helper": "helperhelper"}


def api(user, method, path, body=None):
    req = urllib.request.Request(BASE + path, method=method)
    token = base64.b64encode(f"{user}:{CREDS[user]}".encode()).decode()
    req.add_header("Authorization", "Basic " + token)
    data = None
    if body is not None:
        data = json.dumps(body).encode()
        req.add_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, data) as r:
            raw = r.read()
            return json.loads(raw) if raw else None
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        raise SystemExit(f"{method} {path} as {user}: {e.code} {e.read().decode()[:300]}")


def repo(user, name, private=False):
    return api(user, "POST", "/user/repos", {"name": name, "private": private, "auto_init": True, "default_branch": "main"})


ids = {}
for name in ("alpha", "beta", "quiet"):
    ids[f"ai/{name}"] = repo("ai", name)["id"]
ids["ai/secret"] = repo("ai", "secret", private=True)["id"]
ids["helper/gamma"] = repo("helper", "gamma")["id"]
api("ai", "PUT", "/repos/helper/gamma/subscription")  # ai watches a repo it neither owns nor collaborates on

api("helper", "POST", "/repos/ai/alpha/issues", {"title": "alpha issue one"})
api("helper", "POST", "/repos/ai/alpha/issues", {"title": "alpha issue two (to pin)"})
api("helper", "POST", "/repos/ai/beta/issues", {"title": "beta issue"})
api("helper", "POST", "/repos/helper/gamma/issues", {"title": "gamma issue (to mark read)"})

# pull request from a fork so ai gets a PullRequest-source notification
api("helper", "POST", "/repos/ai/beta/forks", {})
time.sleep(1)
content = base64.b64encode(b"hello from helper\n").decode()
api("helper", "POST", "/repos/helper/beta/contents/hello.txt", {"content": content, "message": "add hello", "branch": "main", "new_branch": "feature"})
api("helper", "POST", "/repos/ai/beta/pulls", {"title": "beta pull request", "head": "helper:feature", "base": "main"})

# notifications are written by a queue, so wait for all five
for _ in range(30):
    notes = api("ai", "GET", "/notifications?all=true&limit=50")
    if len(notes) >= 5:
        break
    time.sleep(1)

for n in notes:
    title = n["subject"]["title"]
    if "to pin" in title:
        api("ai", "PATCH", f"/notifications/threads/{n['id']}?to-status=pinned")
    elif "to mark read" in title:
        api("ai", "PATCH", f"/notifications/threads/{n['id']}?to-status=read")

notes = api("ai", "GET", "/notifications?all=true&limit=50&status-types=unread&status-types=read&status-types=pinned")
print("repo ids:", json.dumps(ids))
for n in sorted(notes, key=lambda n: n["id"]):
    status = "pinned" if n["pinned"] else ("unread" if n["unread"] else "read")
    print(f'  #{n["id"]} {n["repository"]["full_name"]:13} {n["subject"]["type"]:12} {status:7} {n["subject"]["title"]}')
json.dump(ids, open(__file__.replace("seed.py", "ids.json"), "w"))

```

import html, http.cookiejar, json, re, sys, urllib.parse, urllib.request

BASE = "http://localhost:3002"
IDS = json.load(open(__file__.replace("webcheck.py", "ids.json")))


class NoRedirect(urllib.request.HTTPRedirectHandler):
    def redirect_request(self, *a, **k):
        return None


class Session:
    def __init__(self, user, password):
        self.jar = http.cookiejar.CookieJar()
        self.open = urllib.request.build_opener(urllib.request.HTTPCookieProcessor(self.jar)).open
        self.noredir = urllib.request.build_opener(urllib.request.HTTPCookieProcessor(self.jar), NoRedirect).open
        page = self.get("/user/login")
        csrf = re.search(r'name="_csrf" value="([^"]+)"', page)
        form = {"user_name": user, "password": password}
        if csrf:
            form["_csrf"] = csrf.group(1)
        self.open(urllib.request.Request(BASE + "/user/login", urllib.parse.urlencode(form).encode(), headers={"Origin": BASE}))
        assert "notification" in self.get("/notifications"), "login failed"

    def get(self, path):
        with self.open(BASE + path) as r:
            return r.read().decode()

    def post(self, path):
        req = urllib.request.Request(BASE + path, b"", method="POST", headers={"Origin": BASE})
        try:
            with self.noredir(req) as r:
                return r.status, r.headers.get("Location")
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
            return e.code, e.headers.get("Location")


def parse(page):
    table = page.split('id="notification_table"', 1)[1]
    rows = [int(x) for x in re.findall(r'id="notification_(\d+)"', table)]
    count = re.search(r'notifications-unread-count ui label( tw-hidden)?">(\d+)<', page)
    repo_menu = page.split('data-test-id="notification-filter-repo"', 1)[1].split('data-test-id="notification-filter-type"', 1)[0]
    type_menu = page.split('data-test-id="notification-filter-type"', 1)[1].split("</div>\n\t\t\t\t\t</div>", 1)[0]
    label = lambda menu: html.unescape(re.search(r'<span class="text">(.*?)</span>', menu, re.S).group(1).strip())
    items = re.findall(r'<a class="item flex-text-block( selected)?" href="([^"]*)">\s*<span class="tw-flex-1 gt-ellipsis">([^<]*)</span>\s*(<span[^>]*role="img")?', repo_menu)
    purge = re.search(r'<form action="([^"]*/notifications/purge[^"]*)"[^>]*>\s*<button[^>]*title="([^"]*)"', page)
    status_form = re.search(r'action="([^"]*/notifications/status[^"]*)"', page)
    empty = re.search(r'class="empty-placeholder">(.*?)</div>', page, re.S)
    return {
        "rows": rows,
        "unread_count": None if not count or count.group(1) else int(count.group(2)),
        "repo_label": label(repo_menu),
        "type_label": label(type_menu),
        "repo_items": [(name, "dot" if dot else "", "selected" if sel else "", html.unescape(href)) for sel, href, name, dot in items],
        "all_repos_href": html.unescape(re.search(r'<a class="item( selected)?" href="([^"]*)">All repositories', repo_menu).group(2)),
        "type_hrefs": [html.unescape(h) for h in re.findall(r'href="([^"]*)">(?:All types|Issues|Pull requests|Commits|Repositories)<', type_menu)],
        "purge": (html.unescape(purge.group(1)), html.unescape(purge.group(2))) if purge else None,
        "status_form": html.unescape(status_form.group(1)) if status_form else None,
        "empty": re.sub(r"<[^>]+>|\s+", " ", empty.group(1)).strip() if empty else None,
        "empty_links": [html.unescape(h) for h in re.findall(r'href="([^"]*)"', empty.group(1))] if empty else [],
        "clear_button": "Clear filters</a>" in page.split('id="notification_table"', 1)[0],
    }


def show(title, page, *keys):
    p = parse(page)
    print(f"\n== {title}")
    for k in keys:
        print(f"   {k}: {p[k]}")
    return p


def main():
    a, b, gamma, secret = IDS["ai/alpha"], IDS["ai/beta"], IDS["helper/gamma"], IDS["ai/secret"]
    ai = Session("ai", "aiaiaiai")
    step = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "read"
    if step == "read":
        show("Unread tab, no filter", ai.get("/notifications"), "rows", "unread_count", "repo_label", "type_label", "repo_items", "all_repos_href", "purge", "clear_button")
        show("AC1 repo=ai/alpha", ai.get(f"/notifications?repo={a}"), "rows", "unread_count", "repo_label", "purge", "status_form", "clear_button")
        show("AC2 source=pull", ai.get("/notifications?source=pull"), "rows", "unread_count", "type_label")
        show("AC2 source=issue", ai.get("/notifications?source=issue"), "rows", "unread_count", "type_label")
        show("AC3 repo=ai/beta & source=pull", ai.get(f"/notifications?repo={b}&source=pull"), "rows", "unread_count", "repo_label", "type_label", "type_hrefs")
        show("AC3 Read tab, repo=helper/gamma", ai.get(f"/notifications?type=read&repo={gamma}"), "rows", "repo_label")
        show("AC3 Read tab, repo=ai/alpha (pinned only)", ai.get(f"/notifications?type=read&repo={a}"), "rows")
        show("AC4 live refresh (div-only) keeps filter", ai.get(f"/notifications?repo={b}&source=pull&div-only=true&sequence-number=1"), "rows", "repo_label", "type_label")
        p = show("DD3 filter links from page 2 drop page=", ai.get(f"/notifications?repo={a}&page=2"), "rows", "all_repos_href", "type_hrefs")
        print("   any filter link with page=:", any("page=" in h for h in p["type_hrefs"] + [p["all_repos_href"]] + [i[3] for i in p["repo_items"]]))
        show("AC5 source=commit (no match)", ai.get("/notifications?source=commit"), "rows", "empty", "empty_links", "purge")
        show("Unknown values ignored: repo=abc&source=bogus", ai.get("/notifications?repo=abc&source=bogus"), "rows", "repo_label", "type_label", "clear_button")
        helper = Session("helper", "helperhelper")
        for rid, name in ((secret, "ai/secret (private)"), (a, "ai/alpha (public, no notifications)")):
            page = helper.get(f"/notifications?repo={rid}")
            p = show(f"AC6 helper, repo={rid} = {name}", page, "rows", "repo_label", "repo_items", "empty")
            print("   'ai/secret' anywhere in page:", "ai/secret" in page, "| 'secret' anywhere:", "secret" in page.lower())
    elif step == "purge":
        print("\n== AC7 POST /notifications/purge?repo=ai/alpha ->", ai.post(f"/notifications/purge?repo={a}"))
        print("== AC7 POST /notifications/purge?source=pull ->", ai.post("/notifications/purge?source=pull"))
        show("After both purges, Unread tab", ai.get("/notifications"), "rows", "unread_count")
        show("After both purges, Read tab", ai.get("/notifications?type=read"), "rows")


main()

```
